Abysmal

uh-BIZ-mul -- from abysm, an old-fashioned spelling of abyss ('a deep, seemingly bottomless pit') + -al. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

To be abysmal is to be extremely bad or dreadful.

The team's abysmal defense let in nine goals in a single game, the worst performance in the league's history.

Worked Example

Reviews called the film's special effects abysmal, noting that the supposedly terrifying monster looked more like a pile of green garbage bags.

Abysmal doesn't just mean "bad" -- it means bad on a shockingly deep, bottomless scale, as if the quality has no floor.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

dreadful: extremely bad or unpleasant

dismal: depressingly poor in quality

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

superb: excellent; outstanding

excellent: extremely good

Where it sits · how severe the badness is — poor → abysmal → catastrophic

poor vs. abysmal: Poor is a mild, everyday word for below-average quality.

catastrophic vs. abysmal: Catastrophic is reserved for outright disasters, pushing even further than abysmal's bottomless low point.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — abysm-

root — abysm-: an old-fashioned spelling of abyss -- a deep, seemingly bottomless pit or void (you met abyss earlier in this course)

suffix — -al

suffix — -al: having the qualities of; pertaining to

Put it together

Put it together: Abysmal comes from abysm, an old-fashioned spelling of abyss -- the deep, seemingly bottomless pit you already met earlier in this course -- plus -al. Something abysmal is so overwhelmingly bad that it feels bottomless, exactly like the pit its root describes.

Use the root in a new word: abyss

Use the root in a new word: abyss: You already met abyss earlier in this course -- a deep, seemingly bottomless pit or void; abysmal simply adds -al to describe something with that same bottomless quality, but applied to how bad something is.
